newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey details $246 million in new school aid.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey details $246 million in new school aid.

text.p: New Jersey education officials have outlined how they will distribute $246 million in additional school aid mandated by a recent court decision.
The state Supreme Court last month ruled that Gov. Christine Whitman's school financing reforms did not go far enough to equalize spending disparities between rich and poor school districts.
As a result, the state plans to spend about $246 million more in fiscal 1998.

The state Education Department said Jersey City will get the largest increase in aid, with $32 million more than the Whitman administration originally budgeted. Newark will get $24 million and Camden will get $21 million.

Two of the 28 districts the court singled out as "special needs" districts, Hoboken and New Brunswick, will not get any additional money because their spending is already at the average of the richest districts.
